target_columns.name: effective_status
target_columns.transformation: CASE override of source status: Cancelled if status='Cancelled', else Expired if end_date < hardcoded snapshot date 2024-06-30, else Not Yet Active if start_date > snapshot date, else Active

target_columns.name: latest_premium_amount
target_columns.transformation: premium_amount from the premiums row with max collected_date per policy_id (via ROW_NUMBER partitioned by policy_id ordered by collected_date desc), LEFT JOINed so null if no premiums exist

target_columns.name: latest_premium_collected_date
target_columns.transformation: collected_date from the same latest-premium row as latest_premium_amount, LEFT JOINed so null if no premiums exist

quirks: Hardcoded snapshot date '2024-06-30' as a literal in the query -- must be preserved exactly (not replaced with CURRENT_DATE) unless the migration explicitly parameterizes it, since the business purpose is a fixed point-in-time snapshot

WHERE p.start_date <= @SnapshotDate silently excludes policies that start after the snapshot date, even though the CASE expression defines a 'Not Yet Active' status for that scenario -- that branch is dead/unreachable in the current output and migration must decide whether to preserve this filter (dropping future policies) or fix the apparent bug

ROW_NUMBER() tie-breaking on collected_date DESC has no secondary sort key, so if a policy has multiple premium rows with the identical max collected_date, the 'latest' row chosen is nondeterministic -- must pick a stable tie-breaker (e.g. a surrogate id) to make PySpark output reproducible and match-able to the legacy result
LEFT JOIN to premiums means policies with zero premium rows legitimately get NULL latest_premium_amount/collected_date -- must not be coalesced to 0 or dropped

effective_status CASE order matters: Cancelled is checked before date-based conditions, so a Cancelled policy with end_date in the past still reports 'Cancelled' not 'Expired' -- order of WHEN clauses must be preserved exactly in the PySpark translation
